topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, sets the context for the cancer lecture series, and outlines the learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Endogenous Factors, Heredity, and Environmental Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the core nature of cancer as a genetic disease influenced by random endogenous processes, inherited predispositions, and global epidemiological variations.

topics.label: Biological and Chemical Carcinogens: Pathogens, Radiation, and Xenobiotics
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail specific direct and indirect carcinogens—including infectious agents, dietary toxins, UV radiation, and chemical hydrocarbons—and their mechanisms of DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor Initiation, Promotion, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the distinction between cancer initiators and promoters, focusing on chronic inflammation, cellular signaling pathways, and host developmental vulnerability.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying and Testing Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the genomic signatures, epidemiological biobanks, in vivo animal models, and in vitro assays used to evaluate carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Risk-Benefit Analysis and Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by framing carcinogenic exposure in the context of everyday risk-benefit decisions and summarizing the main takeaways.
